title: Codecademy
text:
Codecademy was founded in August 2011 by Zach Sims and Ryan Bubinski.[1] Sims dropped out of Columbia University to focus on launching a venture, and Bubinski graduated from Columbia in 2011.[2] The company, headquartered in New York City, raised $2.5 million in Series A funding in October 2011 and $10 million in Series B funding in June 2012.[1,3] The latest round of funding was led by Index Ventures.[4]

In August 2015, Codecademy partnered with the White House, working to host in-person meet-ups for 600 students from disadvantaged women and minority groups over a twelve-month period.[5,6]

By August 2017, Codecademy's CEO Zach Sims officially announced the launch of the new paid "Pro" product.[7] A "Pro Intensive" paid offering was also launched in August 2017[8] but as of 2020 this product appears to no longer be offered.

In December 2021, Skillsoft announced that it would acquire Codecademy for approximately $525 million in cash and stock.[9] The sale was closed on April 5, 2022.[10]

### Partnerships

In August 2017, Codecademy partnered with Amazon for free Alexa skills training.[11,12]

By October 2018, the company employed 85 people, up from 45 in 2016.[13] It had also raised $42.5 million from groups such as Union Square Ventures and Naspers.[13]

By January 2020, Codecademy had expanded to a suite of languages including C++, C#, Go, Java, JavaScript, Ruby, PHP, Python, R, Swift, and SQL, as well as various libraries, frameworks, and associated subjects.[14] According to their roadmap,[15] Codecademy is slated to release Android Development, ASP.NET, Flask, Kotlin, and TypeScript courses in 2019.
